intro: Troubleshoot display mode and frame pacing without modifying game memory. This Digital Racer guide focuses on decisions a player can check in ordinary gameplay or through official settings, not secret unlocks or promises of certain results. Exact conditions depend on mode, device and current update, so begin with the rules and controls the game actually exposes. Aim for a repeatable process that improves awareness, safety and consistency instead of copying a single dramatic clip.

sections.heading: Define the symptom
paragraphs: Mouse movement that feels delayed differs from stuttering video or intermittent network input. Check whether the delay occurs in menus, the training range or only online fights. This separates display pipeline issues from connection problems.

sections.heading: Compare fullscreen and windowed modes
paragraphs: Use the emulator's supported display options while keeping game resolution and frame settings constant. Note the difference in responsiveness, not only FPS. If a mode causes flicker or black screens, revert before testing additional changes.

sections.heading: Check display refresh settings
paragraphs: Confirm Windows is using the monitor's intended refresh rate. A 144 Hz monitor set to 60 Hz can change the visible experience. Matching a supported frame cap to sustainable performance may feel smoother than a high but unstable setting.

sections.heading: Review synchronization controls
paragraphs: Driver or application synchronization options can influence tearing and delay, but results depend on the display and emulator. Test one option at a time and record frame pacing. Avoid blanket graphics overrides for unrelated programs.

sections.heading: Disable unnecessary overlays
paragraphs: Game bars, performance overlays and recording software may add overhead or capture conflicts. Remove optional overlays one by one while preserving security software. Do not rely on mysterious input DLL files or patched emulator launchers.

sections.heading: Use a repeatable aim test
paragraphs: Move the mouse a similar distance and compare visible response across several tries. If one display mode feels better only during an isolated sample, continue testing. Stability and allowed game operation take priority over unverified latency claims.

sections.heading: Apply this method and compare results
paragraphs: For a reliable comparison, note the present settings and record the symptom before changing anything. Make only one supported adjustment, restart the affected application when appropriate and retest the same situation. Revert changes that worsen stability, security or comfort. A percentage or benchmark without practical improvement is not a good reason to keep a tweak. Use only official game and operating-system controls where possible.
